title: EcoVal: An Efficient Data Valuation Framework for Machine Learning

problem.claim: Strategic decision-making in machine learning initiatives requires quantifying the value of data.

gap.claim: Existing Shapley-value-based data valuation frameworks are computationally expensive because they require repeated model training.

contributions.claim: EcoVal estimates the value of data for machine learning models in a fast and practical manner.
The framework values clusters of similar data points and propagates the cluster value to member points.
The framework determines overall data value by estimating intrinsic and extrinsic value and formulates model performance as a production function.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a formal proof of their valuation technique and an explanation of the principles and mechanisms enabling accelerated performance.
The authors report real-world effectiveness for both in-distribution and out-of-sample data.
The authors report that the code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data valuation is important for strategic decision-making in machine learning.
Existing Shapley-based approaches require costly repeated model training.
EcoVal introduces a fast and practical framework using cluster-level valuation, value propagation, intrinsic and extrinsic value, and a production-function formulation.
The authors provide a formal proof and explain mechanisms associated with accelerated performance.
The method is reported as effective for in-distribution and out-of-sample data and is positioned as addressing efficient valuation at scale.

unknowns: The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or computational savings.
The abstract does not specify the clustering procedure or value-propagation mechanism.
The abstract does not describe the formal proof or its assumptions.
The abstract does not identify the machine learning models or application domains evaluated.
